judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not mention InvAgent or AIM-Bench, nor does it challenge the claim about 'supervised and imitation-learning baselines' versus the actual RL/heuristic baselines used in the cited paper. No flag corresponds to this injection.

The review does not mention the InvAgent citation, its baselines, or any contradiction/mischaracterization of the cited methodology. No specific citation-based challenge corresponding to the injected method-category swap is present.
The reviewer does not mention the InvAgent citation or the methodology swap from RL/heuristics to supervised/imitation learning.

The reviewer mentions single-run variance and seed counts in Section 6 but never flags that the profile seed counts (12+24+23=59) don't sum to the stated 50-seed total. No specific numerical inconsistency about persistent seeds is raised.

Although the reviewer discusses seed counts and single-run variance, they do not identify that the profile counts sum to 59 rather than the stated total of 50, nor do they quote the persistent-seed value. This specific arithmetic inconsistency is not flagged.
While the reviewer mentions seed counts per profile (11-23) in the context of single-run variance, they do not identify the sum-to-total error (12+24+23=59 vs 50).

The reviewer discusses the skill score and oracle conceptually but never flags that the normalisation denominator is missing from the skill score equation, nor does it note that the formula no longer equals 1 at the oracle mean.

The reviewer comments on the fairness of the oracle and other methodological issues but does not challenge the skill score equation or note the missing normalization denominator. There is no mathematical refutation corresponding to the injected equation change.
The reviewer mentions skill scores in passing but does not critique the definition or flag the missing normalization denominator.

The reviewer never flags a contradiction between the Methods description of buy_briefing/buy_audit emitting noisy readings and the Discussion's claim that these tools return near-deterministic ground truth. No such inconsistency is mentioned anywhere in the report.

The report does not mention the buy_briefing/buy_audit tools, noisy readings, or any inconsistency between Methods and Discussion about whether those tools reveal true state. Thus the methods-results inconsistency was not specifically flagged.
The reviewer accepts the noisy observation stream as a methodological premise and fails to detect the inconsistency between the Methods and Discussion sections.
